title.rendered: How to Set up an Offshore Development Center in Ukraine

content.rendered:
Setting up an Offshore Software Development Center (ODC) in another country basically proposes entrepreneurs to start a business from scratch: renting an office, hiring staff (accountants, developers, HR management, office managers), building supply chain, establishing internal corporate culture, buying equipment, as well as paying taxes. However, despite this practice will most likely burn a hole in the CEO’s pocket, it is the most efficient way to improve business operations on the local level and promote it overseas. Let’s see how to set up offshore development center and what you need to know about the peculiarities of this process.

What Is ODC and Why Ukraine?

Offshore Software Development Center (also called R&D Center) is a subsidiary of an existing company that relocates a part of its business operations to another country. Setting up offshore development center can be done either independently, or via the services of a local vendor. The first option is exposed to many challenges and risks since you need to properly analyze the market, identify rental costs, salary rates, the legal ground for business setup, and other peculiarities. Vendor, on the other hand, is the establishment that knows the steps of creating R&D centers in the country, thus can do it for you in a timely manner. Although you may face additional costs for their services, eventually, you will get your subsidiary set up fastly and painlessly.

Ukraine currently has around 110,000 software developers available on the IT market. They mainly have a degree in computer science, are well-aware of technological advancements, and possess an immense level of responsibility and dedication. Take a look at the examples of companies that foresaw the colossal benefits of offshore development center along with Ukrainian professionals.

In 2009, a world-known South Korean corporation Samsung that manufactures electronic devices, opened its R&D center in Ukraine. Started from a small-scope team of developers, these days, the company operates in a skyscraper in the capital city of Ukraine, Kyiv. Along with another 14 development centers in the world, Samsung’s collaboration with Ukrainian specialists enriched the company with profound research services in computer vision, intelligence security, and other corresponding activities.

Another tech giant in the mobile manufacturing industry Huawei created numerous job opportunities for Ukrainian developers in Kyiv. In 2017, a team of 450 people jump-started their operations in consumer electronics, IT solutions, and hardware development.

Quite an interesting collaboration occurred between Google and Ukraine: the first offshore development center was opened in Ukraine in 2019 when Google acquired the Ukrainian subsidiary of CloudSimple company along with all its developers and staff. At the beginning of this year, Google officially announced that CloudSimple is a part of Google Cloud, which means that the corporation will be improving the integrated VMware migration solution with the Ukrainian workforce.

Foreign companies see Ukraine as a desirable destination for setting up offshore development center. In 2008, the overall foreign funding had a 15.6% share in the country’s GDP, which grew up to 25.8% in 2011. These numbers demonstrated a high demand of extending the business to the Ukrainian market, but let’s take a closer look at offshore development center challenges and benefits.

Offshore Development Center Benefits

An impressive statistics of global corporations to invest in creating Development Centers has a chain of advantages. Here are some of them.

  • Costs-Cutting Strategy

A world-known business strategy to hire remote teams is widely applied in both large and small organizations. However, eventually, opening local R&D centers will cost much less than hiring developers separately. Also, depending on the country, the salary rates might be considerably lower than the domestic ones.

  • Competitive Edge

Companies that have not established their recognition on the local market, will benefit from R&D in terms of building a target audience across the world. The development of a product or service in another country enriches the technical potential of the corporation, thus, grants it a competitive advantage among local manufacturers.

  • Talent Pool

In search of suitable candidates, many companies face a dramatic scarcity of necessary specialists on the domestic market, while employment opportunities on overseas markets bring them a vast number of professionals with required skills, experience, and dedication.

  • Technology

Another attractive aspect among offshore development center advantages is that you can discover so much more in a new market. Your products can be developed by professional specialists and scientists who might possess immense experience and knowledge in the innovations that remain undiscovered on your market.

  • Local Taxation Regulations

If your government has established severe measures of regulating your business operations through skyline taxation, you might find a country where taxes will be more appealing and save you a good sum of money.

Offshore Development Center Risks

If your decision falls on starting offshore development center without a vendor, be prepared to face certain risks, which might appear regardless of what country you chose to set in. So here are key things to consider if you want to build an offshore development center on your own.

  • Fierce Competitiveness

You will overcome dramatic losses if the local consumers do not accept your product. Since the world of technologies is growing rapidly, numerous companies are coming up with new proactive ideas every day to satisfy their users’ needs and create an excellent user experience. Therefore, the product you are entering the market with should already have a differential advantage to stand out from ones offered on the market.

  • Team Management

The subsidiary should be treated with more careful and smart management as you will not be able to control it on a daily basis. That is why you can often face exceeded deadlines or the quality which didn’t meet your expectations. Even though R&Ds usually have their internal staff management, the driving interest of team maintenance is on your shoulders.

  • Additional Costs on Implementation

You might save your financial resources on office rent, salaries, and legal-related matters, however, when it comes to implementation, you never know how much time it takes to develop a product, what pitfalls may arise, will it be demanding on the market, the overall sales. Moreover, sometimes, even after product release, it should be returned to the process of development to make changes and improvements according to the feedback from customers.

  • Breaking Points in Workflows

Since you are starting the operations in another country, it is important to understand its culture, employee mentality, and what drives their productivity. Overall, prior to building the R&D development center not only should you investigate the economic and political situation in the country, but also define the weaknesses in the workforce to make sure how to handle the issues.

How to Set up Offshore Development Center

Establishing a whole new company in another country requires a thorough understanding of the market, profound research, and understanding of challenges that might appear. Here are the steps towards creating a winning offshore software development center.

Step 1 – Assess the Market

This step includes the analysis of competitiveness (existing products and their selling power), define the opportunities (do the customers need your product), identify their buying behavior (how much money they are ready to spend to buy your offering). You may understand that local consumers reveal a complete satisfaction of the existing products on the market, so the challenge for you would be to research what beneficial advantage you can offer. This step requires lots of time resources – from 1 month to 1 year.

Step 2 – Virtually Build the Team

Before you actually start hiring, go to the local job platforms to see if you will be able to collect the employees with necessary specialization. Consider the number of people and their positions at least in the first period of time of R&D operations. Also, analyze the salary rates to properly form your budget scope.

Step 3 – Analyze Local Technology Potential

Obviously, the step of analyzing the market of technologies is one of the vital in opening R&D centers. The purpose of the development center is to generate new innovative solutions to the existing or upcoming product, so you need to make sure that the local specialists are well-aware of such.

Step 4 – Understand the Stakeholders

Even tech giants such as Apple and Google have stakeholders for opening R&D centers across the world. These would include government, legal entities, tax regulatory organizations, suppliers, and other parties. All of them are contributing to the overall development processes and facilitate them considerably.

Step 5 – Create a Roadmap and Business Strategy

All the previous steps that you have done so far, should be united into a business strategy which includes setting up short and long term goals, risk management, defining objectives, vision and mission, and financing.

Step 6 – Know the Law

Before your dedicated offshore development center starts operating, you must analyze local legislation to make sure that you follow the regulations. When you finalize your product development, you might have a need to patent it and guarantee the intellectual property is maintained. This is probably one of the toughest steps as you need to properly analyze the details of local jurisdictions to not fall into a trap.

Offshore Development Center Costs

Before building an R&D center, the company thoroughly analyzes the market opportunities and devotes a lion’s share of time on capital development. Namely, investigates the rental costs (considering office location and size), prices on necessary equipment (including office supplies such as lighting, furniture, and coffee machines), working equipment (computers, projectors), local salary rates (from office managers to software developers).
